'''Chandrashekhar Janardan Joshi''' (born July 22, 1953, at [[Wai, Maharashtra]], [[India]]) is an Indian–American [[Experimental physics|experimental plasma physicist]]. He is known for his pioneering work in [[Plasma acceleration|plasma-based particle acceleration]] techniques for which he won the 2006 [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Joshi&first_nm=Chandrashekhar&year=2006|title=2006 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-03-09}}</ref> and the 2023 [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] (with Pisin Chen and James Rosenzweig).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfvén Prize {{!}} European Physical Society – Plasma Physics Division |url=http://plasma.ciemat.es/eps/awards/alfven-prize/ |access-date=2023-10-06 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Joshi was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2014 for contributions to development of laser- and beam-driven plasma accelerators. He is currently Distinguished Professor of Electrical Engineering, the director of the Center for High Frequency Electronics and the head of the Neptune Laboratory for Advanced Accelerator Research at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ee.ucla.edu/people/faculty/faculty-directory/chandrasekhar-joshi|title=Joshi, Chandrashekhar — UCLA Electrical Engineering|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150331014019/http://www.ee.ucla.edu/people/faculty/faculty-directory/chandrasekhar-joshi|archive-date=2015-03-31|access-date=2015-04-15}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=April 2024}}
Joshi had his primary education at Dravid High school, Wai. While in 9th grade, he was selected by 'Pestalozzi Children's village Trust' in England and went to England for his further studies.

He received his [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc.]] (1974) in [[nuclear engineering]] from the [[University of London]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] (1978) in [[applied physics]] from the [[University of Hull]], which are both in the [[United Kingdom]]. Following a two-year stint as a research associate at the [[National Research Council of Canada]], where he worked on laser-plasma interactions, he joined UCLA first as a researcher and became a faculty member since 1988.

== Scientific contributions ==
At UCLA, Joshi has built a strong research group that has done pioneering work in the areas of laser-[[plasma instabilities]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Joshi|first1=C. J.|last2=Corkum|first2=P. B.|date=1995|title=Interactions of Ultra‐Intense Laser Light with Matter|journal=Physics Today|volume=48|issue=1|pages=36–43|doi=10.1063/1.881451|bibcode=1995PhT....48a..36J|issn=0031-9228}}</ref> plasma-based light sources,<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Plasma lamp with dielectric waveguide|country=US|number=6737809|pubdate=2004-05-18|assign=[[Luxim|Luxim Corp.]]|inventor1-last=Espiau|inventor1-first=Frederick M.|inventor2-last=Joshi|inventor2-first=Chandrashekhar J.|inventor3-last=Chang|inventor3-first=Yian}}</ref> [[laser fusion]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Forslund|first1=D. W.|last2=Kindel|first2=J. M.|last3=Mori|first3=W. B.|last4=Joshi|first4=C.|last5=Dawson|first5=J. M.|date=1985|title=Two-Dimensional Simulations of Single-Frequency and Beat-Wave Laser-Plasma Heating|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=54|issue=6|pages=558–561|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.54.558|pmid=10031551|bibcode=1985PhRvL..54..558F}}</ref> and basic plasma experiments. Joshi has made many fundamental contributions to the understanding of extremely [[Nonlinear optics|nonlinear optical]] effects in plasmas.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Filip|first1=C. V.|last2=Narang|first2=R.|last3=Tochitsky|first3=S. Y.|last4=Clayton|first4=C. E.|last5=Joshi|first5=C.|date=2002|title=Optical Kerr switching technique for the production of a picosecond, multiwavelength CO2 laser pulse|journal=Applied Optics|language=EN|volume=41|issue=18|pages=3743–3747|doi=10.1364/AO.41.003743|pmid=12078701|bibcode=2002ApOpt..41.3743F|issn=2155-3165}}</ref> Most notable including his first experimental demonstration of four-wave mixing, stimulated [[Raman scattering|Raman forward instability]], resonant self-focusing, frequency upshifting by ionization fronts and [[resonant interaction|nonlinear coupling]] between electron-plasma waves.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Modena|first1=A.|last2=Najmudin|first2=Z.|last3=Dangor|first3=A.E.|last4=Clayton|first4=C.E.|last5=Marsh|first5=K.A.|last6=Joshi|first6=C.|last7=Malka|first7=V.|last8=Darrow|first8=C.B.|last9=Danson|first9=C.|date=1996|title=Observation of Raman forward scattering and electron acceleration in the relativistic regime|journal=IEEE Transactions on Plasma Science|volume=24|issue=2|pages=289–295|doi=10.1109/27.509992|bibcode=1996ITPS...24..289M|issn=1939-9375}}</ref> His group is best known, however, for developing the field of plasma-based [[Accelerator physics|particle accelerators]] over the past three decades.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Joshi|first1=C.|last2=Katsouleas|first2=T.|date=2003|title=Plasma Accelerators at the Energy Frontier and on Tabletops|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=56|issue=6|pages=47–53|doi=10.1063/1.1595054|bibcode=2003PhT....56f..47J|issn=0031-9228}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Joshi|first1=C.|last2=Mori|first2=W. == Honors and awards ==
Joshi is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society|APS]], [[IEEE]] and [[Institute of Physics|UK Institute of Physics]]. He is also the recipient of the 1996 [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Joshi&first_nm=Chandrashekhar&year=1996|title=1996 John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-03-09}}</ref> (jointly awarded with Christopher E. Clayton)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Clayton&first_nm=Christopher&year=1996|title=1996 John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-03-09}}</ref> as well as the 1997 {{Interlanguage link|USPAS Prize for Achievement in Accelerator Physics and Technology|lt=|de|USPAS Prize for Achievement in Accelerator Physics and Technology|WD=}}.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://uspas.fnal.gov/about/prize/prize-winners.shtml|title=USPAS {{!}} About {{!}} USPAS Prize {{!}} Past Prize Winners|website=uspas.fnal.gov|access-date=2020-03-09}}</ref> He was the APS [[Centennial]] Speaker (1999) and a Distinguished Lecturer in Plasma Physics (2001). He was elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.nae.edu/107872.aspx |title = Professor Chandrashekhar J. Joshi|website=nae.edu|access-date=April 21, 2024}}</ref>

=== Citations ===
* John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research (1996): "''For their pioneering experiments in Plasma Based Accelerator Concepts; particularly for their unambiguous experimental demonstration that electrons can be accelerated to relativistic energies by the beating of two laser beams in a plasma with their frequency difference equal to the plasma frequency.''"<ref name=":1" />
* USPAS Prize for Achievement in Accelerator Physics and Technology (1997): ''"For pioneering experiments on high gradient, laser-driven, plasma beat-wave acceleration."''<ref name=":2" />
* James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics (2006): ''"For his insight and leadership in applying plasma concepts to high energy electron and positron acceleration, and for his creative exploration of related aspects of plasma physics.''"<ref name=":0" />
* Hannes Alfvén Prize (2023, with Pisin Chen and James Rosenzweig): "For proposing, demonstrating and conducting impressive ground-breaking experiments on plasma wakefield accelerators driven by particle beams, thus firmly establishing the new concept of plasma acceleration and their applications in the scientific community."{{citation needed|date=April 2024}}
